fix:
The index already holds the answer this walk is spending 8.5 s to rediscover. `SELECT DISTINCT source_path FROM note_links WHERE target_name = ?` -> EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN: `SEARCH note_links USING INDEX idx_link_target (target_name=?)`. I am NOT calling this clearly safe — it is a decision, not a patch. Switching the cascade from 'walk every file' to 'ask the index' makes the on-disk rewrite only as complete as note_links is, and PJ-207 exists precisely because that index drifts (60/7,824 drift, 798 never indexed). Two honest shapes: (a) index-driven candidate list + the existing full walk kept as an explicit, user-visible 'thorough' path or a background verify; (b) keep the walk but make it cheap — parallelise the per-file read (rayon over the collected paths; each file already takes its own independent per-path gate lock in write_gate::gate_rmw, so there is no shared lock to serialise on) and/or skip the read for files whose size+mtime are unchanged since the last cascade. what: The cascade walker pays a stat syscall per directory entry that the OS already answered: `path.is_dir()` at src-tauri/src/libraries.rs:6802 and the redundant `path.exists()` at libraries.rs:6811.
evidence:
Same Rust replica, two variants over the same tree (10,310 entries, 2,105 md files), alternated to control for cache state:
  baseline (path.is_dir + path.exists): TOTAL 8.729 s cold / 0.388 s warm, of which stat = 752.7 ms cold / 249.0 ms warm
  FASTSTAT (entry.file_type() for is_dir, drop exists()): TOTAL 0.179 s / 0.148 s, of which stat = 2.3 ms / 2.0 ms
The walker already calls `entry.file_type()` one line earlier, at libraries.rs:6796, for the symlink guard — so the is_dir answer is already in hand and is being thrown away, then re-fetched with a full metadata syscall.
cost_estimate: 0.75-0.92 s cold, 0.25-0.36 s warm, per rename. Removable with no behaviour change. Measured stat cost drops 752.7 ms -> 2.3 ms.
fix: In update_links_recursive (libraries.rs:6796-6811): hoist the `entry.file_type()` already fetched for the symlink guard into a single `ft` binding and use `ft.is_dir()` at :6802 instead of `path.is_dir()`; delete the `if !path.exists() { continue; }` at :6811. The exists() check is dead weight — `gate_rmw` (write_gate.rs:662) does `fs::read_to_string(path)` and maps the failure to an Err, which the walker's existing `Err(e)` arm at libraries.rs:6842 already records. A file that vanishes mid-walk is handled identically either way, and the exists() check cannot close the race it looks like it closes (the file can still vanish between the exists() and the read). This is the one fix in this lane that is unambiguously safe.
risk: None identified. Same walk order, same set of files, same outcomes; the only semantic change is that a file deleted between read_dir and read is reported through the `failed` list instead of being silently skipped — arguably more honest, but if silent-skip is wanted, keep it by matching on the io::ErrorKind::NotFound arm.

what: `rename_folder_db_tail` holds the GLOBAL SearchState writer mutex across `migrate_note_db_paths` for EVERY descendant note in ONE acquisition — src-tauri/src/libraries.rs:1803-1812 (`if let Ok(guard) = search_state.db.lock() { ... for new_desc in &md_paths { ... migrate_note_db_paths(conn, ...) } }`).
evidence:
Per-note cost of migrate_note_db_paths measured statement-by-statement on a working copy of his real 327 MB search.db (perf.db -> perfwork.db), on a real Constellation PKM note path, with foreign_keys=ON and the same BEGIN IMMEDIATE / defer_foreign_keys / COMMIT shape the function uses:
  DELETE note_meta dest 1.27 | DELETE note_embeddings dest 0.28 | UPDATE note_meta path 7.35 | UPDATE note_links source 1.98 | UPDATE note_aliases 0.03 | UPDATE note_embeddings 0.01 | DELETE review_schedule 0.35 | UPDATE review_schedule 0.23 | DELETE note_body 0.31 | UPDATE note_body 0.30 | DELETE/UPDATE note_summaries 0.03 | DELETE/UPDATE sources_suggestions 0.24 | DELETE/UPDATE sight_v3_layout 0.13 | DELETE/UPDATE note_state_history 0.03 | COMMIT 7.24  => TOTAL 19.79 ms per note.
Every statement is an index seek — I ran EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN on all of them and there is no full scan of note_meta anywhere in the rename path (no PJ-066 landmine here).
The second half of the same function (libraries.rs:1818-1832) then calls reindex_single_note per descendant, and reindex_single_note takes the same global lock itself (search.rs:12313 `let db = state.db.lock()`) — so the lock is re-acquired N more times.
The Boss has NOT hit this yet: diagnostics.log line 830 shows his one folder rename today was `[rename-folder-tail] START ... descendants=0`.
cost_estimate: 19.79 ms x N descendants held in a SINGLE continuous acquisition of the global writer mutex. For his Constellation PKM (803 notes) that is ~15.9 s during which every other DB caller in the app — search, backlinks, index panel, any save's reindex — is blocked. Bounded arithmetic from a measured per-note cost, not observed live.
fix: Chunk the loop: acquire the lock, migrate a bounded batch (e.g. 50 notes), drop the guard, yield, re-acquire. The function is already detached to spawn_blocking (libraries.rs:1614) and every statement in it is explicitly best-effort, so nothing depends on the whole descendant set moving under one lock — migrate_note_db_paths already opens its own BEGIN IMMEDIATE/COMMIT per note (libraries.rs:1446-1452), so there is no cross-note transaction to preserve. This is the same PJ-066 rule the file already applies elsewhere ('multi-second derived-data commands must not hold the writer lock'), applied to the one loop that still violates it.
risk: Low, but it changes lock granularity: during the gaps another writer can interleave between descendants, so a reader could observe the folder half-migrated. That is already true today between the migrate phase and the reindex phase (the lock is dropped at libraries.rs:1812), so the window is widened, not created. Worth one line of thought before landing; it is not a design change.

what: note_meta_sky_ai / _sky_au back-resolution `UPDATE note_links SET target_cid_cn = …` (added today) firing the UNGUARDED `note_links_outgoing_au` trigger once per updated row. evidence:

INSERT note_meta with name_lower='note' (471 waiting note_links rows): 65.5–70 ms.
Same INSERT with `note_links_outgoing_au` dropped: 4.5 ms.
Same INSERT with ALL note_meta triggers dropped: 0.021 ms.
INSERT name_lower='doi (identifier)' (280 waiting): 49.0 ms → 5.9 ms with the guard.
INSERT name_lower='الإسلام' (54 waiting): 15.9 ms → 1.75 ms.
INSERT a title with 0 waiting links: 0.71 ms (triggers live) vs 0.020 ms (dropped).
Bisect proof it is this statement: with name_lower deliberately set to a non-matching value the SAME insert costs 2.25 ms with every note_meta trigger live; setting name_lower to the real colliding value takes it to 65 ms.
EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN of the back-resolution statement: `SEARCH note_links USING INDEX idx_link_target (target_name=?)` — an index seek, not a scan. The cost is the cascade, not the lookup.

Add a WHEN guard to note_links_outgoing_au so a target_cid_cn-only write does not trigger an outgoing recount it cannot affect:

CREATE TRIGGER note_links_outgoing_au
    AFTER UPDATE ON note_links
    WHEN OLD.source_path IS NOT NEW.source_path
      OR OLD.status      IS NOT NEW.status
      OR OLD.link_type   IS NOT NEW.link_type
    BEGIN … existing body unchanged … END;

Measured with this exact patch applied to the copy: 471-waiting insert 69.9 → 4.61 ms; 280-waiting 45.7 → 5.89 ms; 54-waiting 15.9 → 1.75 ms; 0-waiting unchanged (0.89 → 0.84 ms).

The three columns in the WHEN are exactly that set. Weight/annotation/cid changes correctly stop recomputing counts that do not depend on them.

Its WHERE is `target_name = COALESCE(NEW.name_lower, LOWER(NEW.name))` with no library or path qualifier, so the FIRST note created under a shared title stamps its cid onto EVERY waiting link naming that title anywhere in the universe.
